options.label: We'll help.
options.tooltip: Leave it to us: whatever has gone wrong, we'll put it right before dusk.

nodes.text: Good morning, Kelderby! Good morning, new faces! Today is the festival: a feast on the square, the bell at dusk, the lighthouse lamp over the bay and the castle's fireworks at midnight. Nothing can possibly go wrong.

That? That is everything going wrong at once. The boatwright's cargo boat has turned over in the bay with the feast in it. The cooper's goats are up the terraces. The bell rope has snapped. And the lighthouse lamp went out in the night, and the keeper is up there swearing at it. Pick one. Pick all of them. Be back on this stage by dusk.
How is it going? Don't tell me. Tell me at dusk. Smile at the town.
Hold the street! Nobody touches the cake!
Look at them. Look at all of them. Right. Whatever happened today, that is the festival now. Shall I begin?

options.label: We're going up.
options.tooltip: Climb the tower and light the lamp.

nodes.text: Went out at three this morning. Wick's fine, oil's fine, the lamp is sulking. Also the stairs gave way in three places on the way up, so you'll be jumping. Light it for me and I'll owe you.
A fox. In MY storeroom. With MY key. And now it is off up the road with it, and the fireworks are locked in until somebody catches it.
Ghost stories. Lady Agathe's family say there is a treasure of the old lords somewhere in it. Forty years I have swept that castle, and if there is, it is better hidden than my storeroom key.
The cake is done. Four tiers, candied cherries, a sugar lighthouse on top. It goes on the stage at dusk and nobody breathes on it until midnight.
My dear, I have watched sixty-one of these festivals and every one of them nearly did not happen. Go on. I shall be in the front row tonight.

Older. My husband's family swore the old lords hid their finest arms somewhere in it before the last siege, and never came back for them. Sixty-one years I have lived up there and found nothing but draughts. Perhaps it is true. Nobody knows how one would get at it, if it were.

options.label: We'll row out.
options.tooltip: Take Sverre's boat out into the bay and bring the crates in.

nodes.text: Turned her over on the bar, didn't I. Six crates of the feast are bobbing about out on the shoals, past the deep water, and two of them out past the outer bar; go round by the channel at the harbour end of it. Take the Herring, the boat by the steps; she rows true. They won't stay afloat long once the tide's on them.
Mind the bar. The boats don't, which is how we got here.

options.label: We'll bring them home.
options.tooltip: Fetch wheat from the field and lead the three goats back into this pen.

nodes.text: My three goats are out of the pen. Pearl, the youngest of my nannies, has gone up onto the terraces behind the fishmonger's, into the orchard above the track. Barley, the best milker in Kelderby, is at the wayside spring, a little way up the castle road. And the Admiral, the old billy who undid the latch, is in the orchard out on the farm track. Each of them has a name over its head, and they'll all follow wheat anywhere. The field's out on the farm track.

Hold the wheat up where they can see it and walk slowly. This pen, mind, on the main street: not the sheep's, not the cows'. Once a goat is in here it stays put, so bring them one at a time if you like. When all three are in, drop the latch on the gate.
All three home and the latch down. Pearl, Barley, the Admiral. I have told them all about you.
I have penned the two that are left. I am not going to talk about the other one today.
I fetched them myself in the end. They are waiting somewhere you will see tonight, and I am not saying where.
If you see a goat anywhere it shouldn't be, it's one of mine.

options.label: Give me the bow.
options.tooltip: Take Vidar's bow and arrows and shoot the target in the bell tower.

nodes.text: By-law fourteen: the bell rings at dusk. The rope snapped this morning, and the knot is caught on the archery target up in the tower's opening, where nobody can reach it. I have a bow. I have never once hit anything with it. Three clean hits would shake the knot free.

happening.subject: npc/runa
happening.text: Runa believes her sister's cow is calving, and reaches for her coat.

options.label: Your sister's cow is calving!
options.tooltip: Send Runa off up the farm track to her sister's calving cow, and take the mare while she is gone.

nodes.text: Moss is in the back stable. She can be hired, at the barrel there, for pennies, which the town is handing out today to anyone who mends something. She is not for running down the main street with.
Forge is cold. Holiday. The counter by the door sells what I made this winter, for the town's pennies. And in the back stands an iron man I have been building since the snow.

Iron, all of him, except the head. An iron man's head is a carved pumpkin, face and all, and every pumpkin in Kelderby was cut into a lantern this morning. Put one on the anvil there once the feast's crates are landed, and he will see. The lantern cutters had a barrel of them out at the allotments, past the far end of the quay.
He has his head. He can see. Waking him is the dear part: five pennies at the counter, and he walks down to the square at dusk and stands with whoever needs standing with.
He will be on the square when the sun goes down. Do not ask him to dance.
